briefs.claim_en: Drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice destroys the coronavirus.
briefs.brief_en: Multiple fact-checking organizations and health institutions, including Snopes, FactCheck.org, AFP Fact Check, National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, Hackensack Meridian Health, NDTV Food, CBS News Boston, and Samayam Tamil, state that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice does not destroy the coronavirus or prevent COVID-19. These sources, published between 2020 and 2021, consistently report a lack of scientific evidence to support such claims. While lemons contain vitamin C, it is not sufficient to boost the immune system to protect against or cure viral infections like COVID-19. The acidity of lemon juice is also not effective in killing the virus, as it can survive in acidic environments. The Guardian reported on March 27, 2020, that the UK government urged people to report "dangerous quack cures" for coronavirus, including those involving lemon juice and hot water.
